name: carts
title: Carts
description: What somebody intends to buy, before they commit to it. Deliberately NOT a draft order: an order is a commitment with a number, a customer and a books consequence, and it sits in a sequence people count, while a basket is a browsing artefact that usually gets abandoned. Modelling the basket as a draft order fills that sequence with junk and makes 'how many orders did we take?' unanswerable -- so carts are their own collection with their own short lifetime. A cart is keyed by a session token rather than an account, because requiring somebody to sign in before they can put something in a basket is the single biggest conversion loss in small-business retail; owner_id is stamped only if and when they sign in. checked_out_order_id is what makes checkout idempotent: a cart that already became an order never becomes a second one, however many times a browser retries the request.

fields.name: session_token
fields.label: Session
fields.help: Opaque, client-held, meaningless outside this shop. Not an identity and never a cross-site key: it says which basket, not who.

fields.name: status
fields.label: Status
fields.help: abandoned returns to open because somebody coming back a week later to the same basket is a sale, not a mistake. checked_out is terminal -- the order is the thing to change now.

fields.name: customer_email
fields.label: Email
fields.help: Collected at checkout, not before. It is what an order needs to send a receipt to; an account is offered afterwards, if at all.

fields.name: checked_out_order_id
fields.label: Became Order
fields.help: Stamped when the cart becomes an order. Present means done: one cart, one order, however many times a retry arrives.

fields.name: owner_id
fields.label: Owner
fields.help: The shop's owner while the basket is anonymous; the shopper once they sign in. A cart always belongs to somebody, so permissions have something to filter on.
